question.text: Neha invests Rs. 10,00,000 each in three instruments for 5 years: (A) a debt mutual fund at 7.1% p.a. (returns taxed at her slab on redemption), (B) Equity Mutual Fund at 12% p.a. (LTCG taxed at 12.5% above Rs. 1,25,000 exemption), and (C) Fixed Deposit at 7% p.a. (interest taxed annually at 30% slab). Which option gives the highest after-tax maturity value?

answer.text: Debt mutual fund — approximately Rs. 14.09 lakh pre-tax (lower after slab tax)
Equity Mutual Fund — approximately Rs. 16.83 lakh (highest despite LTCG tax)
Fixed Deposit — approximately Rs. 12.70 lakh (lower due to annual taxation)
Debt fund and Equity MF give the same after-tax value of approximately Rs. 14.09 lakh

explanation.text: The Logic: Equity MF: FV = Rs. 10,00,000 x (1.12)^5 = Rs. 17,62,342. Gain = Rs. 7,62,342. Taxable gain = Rs. 7,62,342 - Rs. 1,25,000 = Rs. 6,37,342. Tax = Rs. 6,37,342 x 12.5% = Rs. 79,668. Net = Rs. 17,62,342 - Rs. 79,668 = approximately Rs. 16,82,674. FD (annual tax): post-tax rate = 7% x (1 - 0.30) = 4.9%; corpus = Rs. 10,00,000 x (1.049)^5 = approximately Rs. 12,70,216. The debt mutual fund at 7.1% pre-tax compounds to Rs. 14,09,118, but the gain is taxed at slab on redemption, leaving it well below the equity option. Equity wins because the higher pre-tax return more than compensates for the LTCG tax. The Trap: Candidates often assume tax-efficiency alone decides the outcome, but a higher pre-tax return differential dominates over a five-year horizon. FD performs worst because interest is taxed every year, shrinking the compounding base each year. Note: Equity LTCG taxation of 12.5% above the Rs. 1,25,000 exemption is the rate the workbook applies to equity-oriented mutual funds; the PPF Rs. 1,50,000 annual cap means PPF cannot accept a Rs. 10,00,000 lump-sum and is therefore replaced here by a debt mutual fund.
